transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Hello! I'm Dora, a clinical conversational agent. I'm calling to check in with you after your cataract surgery. Do you have any questions about your surgery or recovery?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Hi Dora, yes I do have a few questions. First, when can I start doing a little bit of gardening?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You can start with light gardening, such as watering plants or gentle pruning, about 1 week after surgery. However, it's best to avoid bending, heavy lifting, or strenuous activities for a month. Also, be careful not to get any dirt or debris in your eyes. Would you like to know about anything else?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, when can I start using my eye gel for dry eyes again?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You can start using your eye drops again as long as you've been prescribed. If you're running low, your GP should be able to provide some more. You can also use preservative-free eye drops from the pharmacist four times a day to help with dryness. Do you have any other questions about your eye drops or recovery?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thank you! I also wanted to ask, I'm very sensitive to bright light. Is that normal?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.intended: It's common to have some sensitivity to light after cataract surgery, especially if it's bright. Wearing sunglasses when you're outside can help. If the sensitivity is severe or accompanied by pain and redness, we may need to check it further. But if it's just mild and you're finding it a bit brighter than usual, sunglasses should help. Do you have any other questions?
transcript.delivered: It's common to have some sensitivity to light after cataract surgery, especially if it's bright.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: It's also a good idea to wear sunglasses when you're going outside to help with the sensitivity. Do you have any other questions about your recovery or surgery?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, one more question. Should I still have some blurriness by now?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: It's common for the vision to not be completely clear in the first week after surgery, but it should improve quickly and settle down over time. If your vision is still blurry, or getting significantly worse or blurry, we may need to check it to make sure it's okay.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thanks for the information, Dora. I don't have any more questions.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: I'm glad I could help. It sounds like you're on track with your recovery. I just want to check: are all your questions about your cataract surgery recovery answered to your satisfaction?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, they are. Thank you for all the helpful answers!

verdict.label: fail
verdict.reasoning: The agent conveyed `normal_sensitivity_reassurance` in turn 5 ("It's common to have some sensitivity to light after cataract surgery, especially if it's bright.") and `mild_case_advice` in turn 7 ("It's also a good idea to wear sunglasses when you're going outside to help with the sensitivity."). However, `escalation_criteria` was not conveyed at any point in the conversation.
